'''Katabangan''' ('''[[Catanauan, Quezon|Catanauan]] "Ayta"''', also called '''Catanauanin''') is an extinct [[Aeta language]] that was spoken in the [[Bondoc Peninsula]] of [[Quezon Province]], southern Luzon in the [[Philippines]]. It is misspelled ''Katabaga'' in ''[[Ethnologue]]''.

The Katabangan have completely switched to [[Filipino language|Filipino]]. ''Katabangan'' is also used by some people in the Bikol Region to refer to mixed-blood Agta. Zubiri believes it is likely related to [[Inagta Alabat language|Inagta Alabat]] and to the [[Manide language|Manide]] of western and central [[Camarines Norte]].<ref name="ISO-2019-024"/>

==History and status==
The language was originally listed by Garvan (1963: 8).<ref>Garvan, John M. 1963. ''The Negritos of the Philippines''. Wiener Beiträge zur Kulturgeschichte und Linguistik Band XIV. Vienna: Ferdinand Berger Horn. (Published posthumously from field notes taken by Garvan between 1903 and 1924.)</ref> ''Katabaga'' is in fact a misspelling of ''Katabangan'', the name that the people use to refer to themselves. Some people in the Bikol Region also use the term ''Katabangan'' to refer to mixed-blood Agta in the region. Lobel (2013: 92) reports from a 2006 visit that the Katabangan speak only Tagalog. According to Lobel (2013), based on its present-day location, if the Katabangan did in fact once have their own language, it could possibly have been related to Inagta Alabat (see [[Inagta Alabat language]]) and [[Manide language|Manide]].

Louward Allen Zubiri reports that there are 670 individuals in the Katabangan community. The community was granted an ancestral domain title by the government of the Philippines in 2015. There are also families living in [[Mulanay]], [[Gumaca]], [[Lopez, Quezon|Lopez]], and [[Alabat, Quezon|Alabat]].<ref name="ISO-2019-024"/>

==Vocabulary==
Zubiri compares a few Katabangan lexical items remembered by elders and notes clear similarities with [[Inagta Alabat language|Inagta Alabat]] and [[Manide language|Manide]].<ref name="ISO-2019-024">Zubiri, Louward Allen. 2019. [https://iso639-3.sil.org/sites/iso639-3/files/change_requests/2019/CR_Comments_2019-024.pdf ISO 639-3 Change Request 2019-024].</ref>
